neighbours.label: the verb after the second subject in a difficulty contrast that introduces an intensified comparison (X is hard, but Y [can] be even harder)
fire: Learning to drive is stressful, but parking in the city can be even worse.
Starting a business is difficult, but keeping it running can be even harder.
Losing weight is tough, but keeping it off can be harder still.
Moving house is exhausting, but unpacking afterwards can be even more tiring.
Getting into medical school is hard, but finishing it is harder.
Writing code is tricky, yet debugging someone else's code can be far trickier.
Raising one child is demanding, but raising twins can be even more demanding.
Climbing a mountain is dangerous, but descending it can be even riskier.
quiet: Learning to drive takes a few months, and parking is taught in the last lessons.
Starting a business requires a plan, a bank account and some savings.
Losing weight usually involves eating less and walking more each day.
Moving house involves packing boxes and hiring a van for the weekend.
Getting into medical school requires good grades and an interview.
Writing code involves choosing a language and learning its syntax.
Raising one child involves feeding, bathing and reading stories at night.
Climbing a mountain requires ropes, boots and a reliable weather forecast.

notes: Card: 'learning how to pronounce it [is] not', 'giving up sugar [can] be even harder', 'we're [tougher]'. Probe: 'editing it can be even harder' 2.3x max.
